arxiv-2011-06819.title: diagNNose : A Library for Neural Activation Analysis
arxiv-2011-06819.creator: Jaap Jumelet
arxiv-2011-06819.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce diagNNose , an open source library for analysing the activations of deep neural networks. diagNNose contains a wide array of interpretability techniques that provide fundamental insights into the inner workings of neural networks. We demonstrate the functionality of diagNNose with a case study on subject-verb agreement within language models. diagNNose is available at https://github.

arxiv-2208-12748.title: Brain Chains as Topological Signatures for Alzheimer’s Disease
arxiv-2208-12748.creator: Christian Goodbrake, David Beers, Travis B. Thompson, Heather A. Harrington, Alain Goriely
arxiv-2208-12748.description: Abstract Topology is providing new insights for neuroscience. For instance, graphs, simplicial complexes, directed graphs, flag complexes, persistent homology and convex covers have been used to study functional brain networks, synaptic connectivity, and hippocampal place cell codes. We propose a topological framework to study the evolution of Alzheimer’s disease, the most common neurodegenerative disease.

arxiv-2301-08790.title: On the optimal measurement of conversion gain in the presence of dark noise Journal: josaa
arxiv-2301-08790.creator: Aaron Hendrickson, David P. Haefner, Bradley L. Preece
arxiv-2301-08790.description: Abstract Working from a model of Gaussian pixel noise, we present and unify over twenty-five years of developments in the statistical analysis of the photon transfer conversion gain measurement. We then study a two-sample estimator of the conversion gain that accounts for the general case of non-negligible dark noise.

arxiv-2401-13810.title: Automated Root Causing of Cloud Incidents using In-Context Learning with GPT-4
arxiv-2401-13810.creator: Xuchao Zhang, Supriyo Ghosh, Chetan Bansal, Rujia Wang, Minghua Ma, Yu Kang, Saravan Rajmohan Microsoft {xuchaozhang, supriyoghosh, chetanb, rujiawang, minghuama, yu.kang, saravan.rajmohan}@microsoft.com
arxiv-2401-13810.description: Abstract . Root Cause Analysis (RCA) plays a pivotal role in the incident diagnosis process for cloud services, requiring on-call engineers to identify the primary issues and implement corrective actions to prevent future recurrences. Improving the incident RCA process is vital for minimizing service downtime, customer impact and manual toil.

arxiv-2412-02412.title: VISTA: A Panoramic View of Neural Representations
arxiv-2412-02412.creator: Tom White
arxiv-2412-02412.description: Abstract We present VISTA (Visualization of Internal States and Their Associations), a novel pipeline for visually exploring and interpreting neural network representations. VISTA addresses the challenge of analyzing vast multidimensional spaces in modern machine learning models by mapping representations into a semantic 2D space. The resulting collages visually reveal patterns and relationships within internal representations.

arxiv-2509-25313.creator: Alek Bedroya, Paul J. Steinhardt
arxiv-2509-25313.description: Abstract In this work, we point out a contradiction between holography and scale-separated AdS (i.e. parametrically large mass gap) in string theory, making the standard assumption that the holographic CFT describes the IR degrees of freedom on a brane that decouple from gravity.

pmc-10707428.title: Chemical Structure Diversity and Extensive Biological Functions of Specialized Metabolites in Rice
pmc-10707428.creator: Huiwen Zhou, Jinjin Zhang, Liping Bai, Jiayi Liu, Hongdi Li, Juan Hua, Shihong Luo, Karel Doležal, Daniela Trono
pmc-10707428.description: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is thought to have been domesticated many times independently in China and India, and many modern cultivars are available. All rice tissues are rich in specialized metabolites (SPMs). To date, a total of 181 terpenoids, 199 phenolics, 41 alkaloids, and 26 other types of compounds have been detected in rice.

pmc-11429503.title: The correlation between social adaptability and academic procrastination of undergraduate nursing students: the mediating role of resilience
pmc-11429503.creator: Yang Guo, Fangfang An, Anqi Li, Jie Yao, Xiaojie Sun
pmc-11429503.description: BackgroundHow to mobilize nurses students' learning initiative, reduce the incidence of academic procrastination, and improve their social adaptability is a key factor in lowering nursing brain drain and improving nursing quality.ObjectiveTo explore the mediating role of resilience in the correlation between social adaptability and academic procrastination of undergraduate nursing students.MethodsThis study is a cross-sectional survey.

pmc-11489178.description: Malignant transformation is concomitant with excessive activation of stress response pathways. Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are stress-inducible proteins that play a role in folding and processing proteins, contributing to the non-oncogene addiction of stressed tumor cells. However, the detailed role of the HSP family in osteosarcoma has not been investigated.

pmc-11827839.title: PINK1 is a target of T cell responses in Parkinson’s disease
pmc-11827839.creator: Gregory P. Williams, Antoine Freuchet, Tanner Michaelis, April Frazier, Ngan K. Tran, João Rodrigues Lima-Junior, Elizabeth J. Phillips, Simon A. Mallal, Irene Litvan, Jennifer G. Goldman, Roy N. Alcalay, John Sidney, David Sulzer, Alessandro Sette, Cecilia S. Lindestam Arlehamn
pmc-11827839.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. While there is no curative treatment, the immune system’s involvement with autoimmune T cells that recognize the protein α-synuclein (α-syn) in a subset of individuals suggests new areas for therapeutic strategies.

pmc-12391429.title: A faculty performance evaluation model based on MACBETH and fuzzy filter ranking methods
pmc-12391429.creator: Min Tao, Quanxin Chen, Wenyan Yan, Xiong Wang
pmc-12391429.description: The establishment of a robust faculty performance evaluation system has become a research hotspot, as it is crucial for the continuous improvement and sustainable development of higher education institutions. However, according to available literature, the need for an easy-to-use management tool for faculty performance evaluation—one that accounts for professional tracks—within the context of China’s application-oriented universities remains unaddressed.

pmc-12623342.title: Climate concerns for clinicians: evaluating harmful algal bloom knowledge and educational opportunities for health care provider students
pmc-12623342.creator: Alexander Lund, Carrie McNair, Chelsea McGowen, Janel Lowman, Robert Sobol, Michael Parsons, Jennifer Pierce
pmc-12623342.description: With increasing incidence of harmful algal blooms (HABs) and their associated illnesses such as ciguatera poisoning (CP), there is need for educating current and future clinicians. This study sought to assess medical and physician assistant (PA) students' knowledge, attitudes, and beliefs toward HABs and their related illnesses.

pmc-12728238.title: Exploration of the potential of genomic editing in the treatment of congenital adrenal hyperplasia
pmc-12728238.creator: Lara E. Graves, Sharntie Christina, Kathryn L. Mullany, Ian E. Alexander, Henrik Falhammar
pmc-12728238.description: Despite life-saving glucocorticoids, therapeutic options for congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) remain sub-optimal. Adrenal crisis continues to be the highest cause of mortality in individuals with CAH and even with recommended treatment regimens complications from the disease and treatments themselves persist. These patients have limited treatment options and advanced therapeutics could be a solution.

pmc-13464069.title: IFI30 reprograms glioblastoma-associated macrophage and induces immune evasion by MAFF/PTGS2 pathway
pmc-13464069.creator: Sen Zhang, Wenlin Chen, Liwen Ren, Jie Yi, Xiangjin Zheng, Yihui Yang, Hong Yang, Guanhua Du, Wan Li, Yu Wang, Jinhua Wang
pmc-13464069.description: In recent years, immunotherapy has shown obvious advantages in treating cancers. The close interaction between cancer cells and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME) underlies the progression of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). However, there are no effective immune-related targets against GBM.

pmc-13495094.title: Somatic DICER1-mutated Sertoli–Leydig cell tumor in a postmenopausal woman: eight years of peritoneal relapse managed with cytoreductive surgery and HIPEC – a case report
pmc-13495094.creator: Emily Frances Brown, Katrina Tang, Ruwanthi Wijayawardana, Vivek Arora, Winston Liauw, Lawrence Kasherman
pmc-13495094.description: Sertoli–Leydig cell tumors are rare ovarian sex cord–stromal tumors that usually arise in young women and are often hormonally active. Intraperitoneal dissemination and relapse are uncommon, and recurrence patterns in postmenopausal women are poorly characterized. This report describes a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman with a poorly differentiated, estrogen receptor-negative, non-functional Sertoli–Leydig cell tumor.

pmc-13679102.title: Unilateral flywheel resistance training versus traditional resistance training for change-of-direction performance in elite soccer players: a randomised controlled trial
pmc-13679102.creator: Ziqi Han, TianLiang Zhao, ZhiWei Wen, Tao Yang, Yue Dou, JiaHui Hu, Bo Zhang, DingMeng Ren
pmc-13679102.description: BackgroundSoccer requires frequent high-intensity decelerations, braking actions, and multidirectional re-accelerations. Flywheel resistance training may provide a braking-oriented inertial stimulus that is relevant to change-of-direction (COD) performance. However, randomised controlled evidence directly comparing unilateral flywheel resistance training with unilateral traditional resistance training in high-level soccer players remains limited.

pmc-13719521.title: Germline genetic risk and prostate cancer–specific mortality in a population-based incident cohort
pmc-13719521.creator: Lucy Lu, Julian Xu, Zhuqing Shi, Valentina Engelmann, Huy Tran, Jun Wei, Annabelle Ashworth, Brandon Cornell, Christopher Pieczonka, William B. Isaacs, S. Lilly Zheng, Brian T. Helfand, Jun Luo, Jianfeng Xu, Jim Lu
pmc-13719521.description: BackgroundMultiple germline variants are associated with prostate cancer (PCa) susceptibility and aggressive features; however, their value for predicting prostate cancer–specific mortality (PCSM) at the time of diagnosis remains uncertain, particularly among men with clinically localized disease.MethodsWe evaluated associations between germline risk factors and PCSM among 14,644 men with incident PCa in the UK Biobank.

uslaw-usc-t10-s435.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part I (Organization And General Military Powers); Chapter 21 (Department Of Defense Intelligence Matters); Subchapter II (Intelligence Commercial Activities). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Lawful Activities.— Nothing in this subchapter authorizes the conduct of any intelligence activity that is not otherwise authorized by law or Executive order. (b) Domestic Activities.— Personnel conducting commercial activity.
